rationale: B wins because it finds the third real story hiding in the update: "Anker says its home battery skips the rewiring — installers will decide if that's true." A is competent, but it burns two slots on versions of the same category leap: "The power-bank company just built a whole-home battery" and "Why a phone-charger giant is betting on home energy storage." That is not fatal, but it is exactly how decent angle sets get padded into mediocrity.
gaps_in_A: "The power-bank company just built a whole-home battery" and "Why a phone-charger giant is betting on home energy storage" overlap too much. Brand-trust and corporate-strategy are different wrappers, but the protagonist and core tension are nearly the same.

A misses the strongest technical-claim angle. It buries "installs without major electrical rewiring" as proof inside the Tesla angle instead of making installers/electricians stress-test it as its own story.

"Anker naming Tesla Powerwall as direct competition" overstates the facts. The update says Anker competes with Tesla Powerwall; it does not say Anker named or explicitly positioned itself against Tesla.

"deploying capital into an unfamiliar, competitive category" and "capital-intensive" are plausible, but not supplied. Without investment size, R&D spend, or hiring, this is strategy vapor with a nicer tie.
gaps_in_B: "a brand known for $20 chargers" is invented color. The update says phone chargers and power banks, not price point.

"a purchase measured in thousands of dollars and decades on the wall" outruns the facts. Pricing is only partially disclosed and warranty terms are not detailed, so do not smuggle in a decade-scale ownership claim.

"not for solar trade press (they don't care about Anker's brand journey)" is too absolute. Some solar trade desks may care about a major electronics maker entering residential storage; narrow it without pretending the whole beat is allergic to strategy.
